mainTopic: Why no one answers אמן in the מקדש, and how the כהן גדול reads from the תורה on יום כיפור
overview: The גמרא explains why blessings in the מקדש work differently: people there do not answer אמן. A ברייתא brings two halves of a פסוק in נחמיה. The first half shows that אמן is not said in the מקדש, and the second shows that every blessing there gets its own praise instead. Then a new משנה describes the ברכות כהן גדול on יום כיפור. The ספר תורה is passed up a chain of officials to the כהן גדול. He reads two sections from ויקרא, says a third from במדבר by heart, and then recites eight ברכות. The גמרא first suggests that this teaches a student may be honored in front of his teacher, but אביי rejects that because the whole chain honors the כהן גדול. Next the גמרא asks how the כהן גדול could have been sitting, since only kings from בית דוד may sit in the עזרה. It answers that the reading was in the עזרת נשים. A ברייתא then challenges this answer by saying the reading was in the עזרה, and that challenge continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Why is the Temple practice so different?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the blessings in the מקדש are handled so differently from blessings elsewhere.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the מקדש has its own special way of saying and answering blessings. This short question sets up the answer that comes right after.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The discussion just before this described a different, longer style of blessing in the מקדש. Now the גמרא wants the reason behind that difference.

keyTerms.meaning: And why all this? (Why so different?)

phrases.english: And why all this?
phrases.notes: He's asking why the מקדש has such a different way of blessing from everywhere else.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the special מקדש practice described just before this section.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason the מקדש uses a different blessing practice.

steps.title: Because אמן is not answered in the Temple
steps.stepSummary: The reason is that in the מקדש people do not answer אמן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because one does not answer אמן in the מקדש.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers: in the מקדש nobody says אמן after a blessing. That is why things are done differently there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Outside the מקדש, a blessing ends and everyone answers אמן. Because that response is not used in the מקדש, the blessings there need a different structure and a different response.

keyTerms.meaning: The usual response after hearing a blessing

steps.whatToRemember: In the מקדש, people did not answer אמן after blessings.

phrases.english: Because one does not answer "amen" in the Temple.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The מקדש practice differs because אמן is not answered there.

steps.title: A פסוק shows that אמן is not said in the Temple
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא proves from a פסוק in נחמיה that אמן is not answered in the מקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: From where do we know that one does not answer אמן in the מקדש? Because it says: "Stand up and bless ה׳ your God from everlasting to everlasting."
steps.whatsHappening: A ברייתא gives a source for the rule from step 2. It quotes a פסוק where the people in the מקדש bless ה׳ "from everlasting to everlasting."
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule that there is no אמן in the מקדש now has support from a פסוק. The people there say a full blessing of ה׳ instead of the short word אמן.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
From where do we know that one does not answer "amen" in the Temple?
As it says: "Stand up and bless ה׳ your God
from everlasting to everlasting."

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: מִנַּיִן שֶׁאֵין עוֹנִין ״אָמֵן״ בַּמִּקְדָּשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a פסוק-based source for the rule stated in step 2.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that אמן is not answered in the מקדש.
steps.raayaSupportSource: נחמיה 9:5: קומו ברכו את ה׳ אלהיכם מן העולם עד העולם.

steps.title: Every blessing in the Temple gets its own praise
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues with the rest of the פסוק: each blessing in the מקדש is answered with its own praise.
steps.simpleTranslation: And from where do we know that every single blessing gets praise? Because it says: "And let them bless Your glorious Name, which is exalted above all blessing and praise." This means: for each and every blessing, give Him praise.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא brings the second half of the same פסוק. It shows that in the מקדש, every blessing gets its own words of praise.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 3 showed what the מקדש does not have, which is אמן. This step shows what it has instead: a separate praise for each blessing. The words "על כל ברכה ותהלה" are read as "on every blessing, praise."
steps.whatToRemember: In the מקדש there is no אמן. Instead, every single blessing is answered with its own praise of ה׳.

phrases.aramaic: וּמִנַּיִן שֶׁעַל כׇּל בְּרָכָה וּבְרָכָה תְּהִלָּה —
phrases.english: And from where do we know that for each and every blessing there is praise?
As it says: "And let them bless Your glorious Name,
phrases.notes: נחמיה 9:5, the same פסוק as before.

phrases.english: which is exalted above all blessing and praise."

phrases.aramaic: עַל כׇּל בְּרָכָה וּבְרָכָה תֵּן לוֹ תְּהִלָּה.
phrases.english: For each and every blessing, give Him praise.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִנַּיִן שֶׁעַל כׇּל בְּרָכָה וּבְרָכָה תְּהִלָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא with the second half of the same פסוק and adds what replaces אמן.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that each blessing in the מקדש receives its own praise.
steps.raayaSupportSource: נחמיה 9:5: ויברכו שם כבודך ומרומם על כל ברכה ותהלה.

steps.title: The Torah scroll is passed up to the High Priest
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה describes the ברכות כהן גדול. First, the ספר תורה is handed up a chain of officials to the כהן גדול.
steps.simpleTranslation: How are the blessings of the כהן גדול done? The synagogue attendant takes a ספר תורה and gives it to the head of the synagogue. The head of the synagogue gives it to the סגן, and the סגן gives it to the כהן גדול.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It explains how the כהן גדול reads the תורה on יום כיפור, starting with how the scroll is passed to him step by step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The scroll does not go straight to the כהן גדול. It moves up from the lowest official to the highest, one person after another.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה (marks the start of a משנה)
The deputy of the כהן גדול

steps.confusionAlert: Here חזן means the attendant who handles the scroll, not the person who leads the davening as the word is used today.

phrases.english: MISHNAH: The blessings of the High Priest, how are they done?
The synagogue attendant takes a Torah scroll
and gives it to the head of the synagogue,
and the head of the synagogue gives it to the deputy,
and the deputy gives it to the High Priest,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה on a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ספר תורה is handed from the חזן to the ראש הכנסת, then to the סגן, then to the כהן גדול.

steps.title: The High Priest reads, rolls the scroll, and recites a third section by heart
steps.stepSummary: The כהן גדול reads אחרי מות and אך בעשור from the scroll. He rolls it up, holds it, announces that more is written there, and says ובעשור from במדבר by heart.
steps.simpleTranslation: The כהן גדול stands, receives the scroll, and reads "אחרי מות" and "אך בעשור." Then he rolls up the תורה, holds it against his chest, and says: "More than what I read before you is written here." He reads "ובעשור" from ספר במדבר by heart.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה describes the כהן גדול's reading. He reads two sections from the scroll, then says the third section from memory instead of reading it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two sections from ויקרא are read from the scroll itself. The third, from במדבר, is said by heart after the scroll is rolled up. Before that, the כהן גדול tells the people that the scroll contains more than he read.

keyTerms.meaning: The יום כיפור section in ויקרא 16
The יום כיפור section in ויקרא 23

steps.whatToRemember: The כהן גדול reads two sections from the scroll (אחרי מות and אך בעשור). He says the third (ובעשור in במדבר) by heart.

phrases.english: And the High Priest stands and receives it,
and reads "After the death" and "But on the tenth."
And he rolls up the Torah and places it on his chest,

phrases.aramaic: וְאוֹמֵר: יָתֵר מִמַּה שֶּׁקָּרִיתִי לִפְנֵיכֶם כָּתוּב כָּאן.
phrases.english: and says: More than what I have read before you is written here.
"And on the tenth" in the Book of Numbers, he reads by heart.
phrases.notes: חומש הפקודים is ספר במדבר; the section is במדבר 29:7–11.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה from the moment the כהן גדול receives the scroll.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The כהן גדול reads אחרי מות and אך בעשור from the scroll, rolls it up, declares that more is written, and recites ובעשור from במדבר by heart.

steps.title: The eight blessings after the reading
steps.stepSummary: The משנה ends by listing the eight ברכות the כהן גדול says after reading from the תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: After the reading, he says eight blessings: about the Torah, the Temple service, thanksgiving, forgiveness of sin, the Temple, the Jewish people, the priests and Jerusalem, and the rest is prayer.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה finishes its description of the כהן גדול's reading. It lists the eight ברכות he says afterward.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 6 described what he reads. Now the משנה adds what he says after the reading. Most of the ברכות are about the מקדש and its people. The words 'the rest is prayer' mean he ends with general prayers and requests.
steps.whatToRemember: The משנה ends here. The כהן גדול reads, then says eight ברכות, then adds his own prayers.

phrases.english: And he recites over it eight blessings:
on the Torah, and on the Temple service,
and on thanksgiving, and on forgiveness of sin,
and on the Temple, and on the Jewish people,
and on the priests, and on Jerusalem,
and the rest is prayer.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the משנה's description that began in steps 5-6.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: After the reading, the כהן גדול says eight specific ברכות and then adds general prayer.

steps.title: Learning that a student may be honored before his teacher
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests a lesson from the משנה: honor may be given to a student in front of his teacher.
steps.simpleTranslation: You can learn from this that honor may be given to a student in the presence of the teacher.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens its discussion with a proposed lesson. It points to the scroll being passed up through officials in front of the כהן גדול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, the חזן הכנסת, the ראש הכנסת and the סגן each hold the scroll before the כהן גדול gets it. Those officials get honor even though the greater person is standing right there. So the גמרא suggests it is fine to honor a student when his teacher is present.

keyTerms.meaning: in the presence of the teacher

phrases.english: Gemara:
You can learn from this
that honor is given to a student in the presence of the teacher.
phrases.notes: 'This' points to the officials in step 5 who held the scroll before it reached the כהן גדול.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a general rule from the chain of officials described in step 5.
steps.raayaObject: Honor may be given to a student in the presence of his teacher.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's chain of officials passing the scroll up to the כהן גדול.

steps.title: אביי: the whole chain honors the כהן גדול
steps.stepSummary: אביי rejects the proof. The passing of the scroll is entirely meant to honor the כהן גדול.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: It is all for the honor of the כהן גדול.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי pushes back on the lesson from step 8. He says the case shows nothing about honoring students.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The scroll moves up from one official to a more important one, and the most important of all is the כהן גדול. This shows that he stands above everyone else. So the officials are not being honored at his expense, and no general rule can be learned from here.
steps.whyThisMatters: The rule about honoring a student before his teacher is left without proof from this משנה.

phrases.english: Abaye said:

phrases.aramaic: כּוּלַּהּ מִשּׁוּם כְּבוֹדוֹ דְּכֹהֵן גָּדוֹל הוּא.
phrases.english: All of it is for the honor of the High Priest.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: כּוּלַּהּ מִשּׁוּם כְּבוֹדוֹ דְּכֹהֵן גָּדוֹל הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the inference made in step 8.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from the chain of officials only.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The officials are not being honored. The process exists to raise the honor of the כהן גדול.

steps.title: How could the כהן גדול have been sitting?
steps.stepSummary: The word 'stands' suggests the כהן גדול was sitting, but only kings from בית דוד may sit in the עזרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says the כהן גדול 'stands and receives and reads.' 'Stands' implies he was sitting before. But it was taught that no one may sit in the Temple courtyard except kings from the house of David, as the פסוק says: 'King David came and sat before ה׳.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a line from the משנה and raises a problem with the word 'stands.' It contrasts this with a known rule that sitting in the עזרה is forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the משנה says he 'stands,' that means he was sitting until then. But a ברייתא teaches that only kings from בית דוד may sit in the עזרה, based on דוד sitting before ה׳. So how could the כהן גדול have been sitting there?

keyTerms.meaning: kings from the house of David

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying the כהן גדול sat. It is asking how the משנה's wording could suggest he did, since sitting in the עזרה is forbidden.

phrases.aramaic: וְכֹהֵן גָּדוֹל עוֹמֵד וּמְקַבֵּל וְקוֹרֵא וְכוּ׳.
phrases.english: 'And the High Priest stands and receives and reads,' etc.
'Stands' implies that he was sitting?
But didn't the master say:
There is no sitting in the Temple courtyard
except for kings of the house of David alone,
as it is said:
'Then King David came and sat before ה׳,'
'and he said: Who am I,' etc.!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new question about the משנה's wording, separate from the honor discussion in steps 8-9.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'Stands' implies he was sitting before. But sitting in the עזרה is allowed only for kings from בית דוד, so the כהן גדול could not have been sitting there.

steps.title: The reading took place in the women's courtyard
steps.stepSummary: Using רב חסדא's statement, the גמרא answers that the כהן גדול read in the עזרת נשים, where sitting is allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רב חסדא said, it was in the women's courtyard. Here too, it was in the women's courtyard.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from Step 10. The כהן גדול could sit because the reading was in the עזרת נשים, not in the main עזרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ban on sitting (except for kings from בית דוד) applies only in the main עזרה. The עזרת נשים does not have that holiness, so sitting there is fine. The גמרא takes an answer רב חסדא gave elsewhere and applies it here.

keyTerms.meaning: The women's courtyard, an outer courtyard of the בית המקדש with less holiness
As (someone) said; brings an existing statement to answer the question

phrases.english: As Rav Ḥisda said:
in the women's courtyard,
here too, it was in the women's courtyard.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 10 about the כהן גדול sitting in the עזרה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the location of the case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The reading was in the main עזרה, where only kings from בית דוד may sit.
steps.terutzMaskana: The reading was in the עזרת נשים, where anyone may sit.

steps.title: A ברייתא says the reading was in the courtyard
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the answer with a ברייתא saying the reading took place in the עזרה. רבי אליעזר בן יעקב says it was on the הר הבית.
steps.simpleTranslation: They raised an objection: Where do they read from it? In the courtyard. רבי אליעזר בן יעקב says: on the Temple Mount, as it is said:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that seems to contradict the answer it just gave. The ברייתא's first opinion says the reading was in the עזרה, which sounds like the main courtyard, not the עזרת נשים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the reading was in the main עזרה, the problem of sitting comes back. The ברייתא also brings רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, who places it on the הר הבית. He begins to bring a פסוק as his source, which the גמרא quotes next.

keyTerms.meaning: They raised an objection, usually from a ברייתא
The courtyard of the בית המקדש
The Temple Mount, the area surrounding the courtyards
As it is said; introduces a פסוק

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two places. עזרה here sounds like the holy inner courtyard. The עזרת נשים is a separate outer courtyard, and that difference is what the challenge is about.

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
And where do they read from it?
phrases.notes: "It" is the ספר תורה the כהן גדול reads from on יום כיפור.

phrases.english: In the courtyard.
Rabbi Eliezer ben Ya'akov says:
On the Temple Mount, as it is said:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of Step 11 that the reading was in the עזרת נשים.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's answer, applied here, that the reading took place in the עזרת נשים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא says the reading was in the עזרה, which sounds like the main courtyard, where sitting is forbidden. So the problem of sitting comes back.
